fields.quote: Invalidate after a successful write, with a remaining reader race
fields.rationale: after() awaits db.write then cache.delete; after.failedWrite leaves cachedAfterUpdate 'old' when write rejects, so deletion is tied to fulfillment. after.lateSnapshot.cached and nextRead are 'old' while stored is 'new', which is the remaining reader race. Probe assert: 'an older snapshot can refill the cache after invalidation'.
source.json title is 'Moss Catalog: invalidate a cache entry after writing'. The displayed label matches that source name. It is not a program-behavior claim beyond naming.

fields.quote: Post-write deletion removes cache fills that finish during the write, but an older in-flight snapshot can refill the cache afterward.
fields.rationale: after.fillDuringWrite has cached null and nextRead 'new', versus before.fillDuringWrite cached 'old' and nextRead 'old'. Probe assert: 'post-write deletion removes a cache fill that completed during the write'. after.lateSnapshot has cached 'old' and nextRead 'old' after stored is 'new'. These are the gated interleavings in probe.mjs, not a proof for other runtimes.

fields.quote: Early deletion left a window for stale fills
fields.rationale: before() does cache.delete then await db.write. before.fillDuringWrite has overlappingRead 'old', cached 'old', nextRead 'old' while stored becomes 'new'. That is the early-delete fill window.

fields.quote: The old update deleted the cached entry before awaiting the database write. A cache miss could read and cache the old stored value during that wait.
fields.rationale: source.before and functions.mjs before(): cache.delete(key); await db.write(key, value). overlapping(fn, false) starts the write, then read() on an empty Map, captures stored while it is still 'old', cache.set, then the write commits. before.fillDuringWrite matches: overlappingRead 'old', cached 'old'.
Chapter label. Not a claim about the source, functions, or probes.

fields.quote: Delete only after the write fulfills
fields.rationale: after() is await db.write then cache.delete. If write throws, delete does not run: after.failedWrite.cachedAfterUpdate is 'old' and error is 'write'. Contract: rejection leaves the stored value unchanged (failedWrite.stored is 'old').

fields.quote: The changed update deletes after the write succeeds. It removes an old cache fill that completed during the write. A failed write leaves an existing cached entry in place. In the sequential example, the next read sees the new stored value.
fields.rationale: Four modeled facts: (1) after() deletes only after write fulfillment. (2) after.fillDuringWrite.cached is null and nextRead is 'new' after overlappingRead 'old' — the fill during the write is gone. (3) sequential(fn, true) starts with Map [['key','old']]; after.failedWrite.cachedAfterUpdate is 'old'. (4) after.sequential.nextRead is 'new'. The fill-removal sentence is the fillDuringWrite schedule, not every possible interleaving.
Chapter label. Not a claim about the source, functions, or probes.

fields.quote: An older snapshot can arrive after deletion
fields.rationale: overlapping(fn, true) captures stored while it is 'old', then after() commits 'new' and cache.delete, then the reader cache.set of that snapshot. after.lateSnapshot.cached is 'old' after stored is 'new'.

fields.quote: The author says concurrent stale reads are removed, but read is unchanged. The modeled reader captures the old database value, waits through the update and deletion, then caches that old value. A subsequent read returns the stale entry. The change supplies no generation check or in-flight reader synchronization.
fields.rationale: source.body: 'The author says invalidating after the write removes stale cache reads, including concurrent readers.' Contract and source.unchanged: read is unchanged; no generation check or in-flight reader synchronization. lateSnapshot path: snapshot = stored ('old'), update runs to completion, then cache.set(snapshot). after.lateSnapshot.overlappingRead 'old', cached 'old', nextRead 'old'. Cancellation and TTL from the same contract are not mentioned here.
Chapter label. Not a claim about the source, functions, or probes.

Contrast of fillDuringWrite.nextRead: before 'old', after 'new'. lateSnapshot.nextRead stays 'old' for both. The change closes the during-write fill window in this model, not the late-snapshot window.

fields.quote: Moving deletion after a successful write closes the window for fills that finish during that write. It does not prevent stale results from overlapping readers or late cache fills.
fields.rationale: First sentence matches after.fillDuringWrite (cached null, nextRead 'new') versus before.fillDuringWrite (cached 'old', nextRead 'old'). Second sentence matches after.fillDuringWrite.overlappingRead 'old' and after.lateSnapshot cached/nextRead 'old'. 'Closes the window' is the gated fillDuringWrite case on one Map.
